name: Coffee table, end table or console
tagline: A top, legs or a frame, and sometimes a glass panel or a lower shelf. Usually the quickest build in the house.
covers: Tables with a glass top or shelf
peopleNote: One person, unless there is glass involved, in which case two.

tools.n: Suction cup lifter or two people
tools.why: Only if there is a glass top or shelf.

provided: Rubber or suction pads for glass
before: Work with the top upside down on the box. Same as every table.
If there is glass, leave it in its packaging until the very last step, and never set it on a hard floor on its edge.
Check whether the legs are angled. Many modern tables have splayed legs that must all lean the same way.
safety: Tempered glass shatters into fragments if you knock an edge or over-tighten a clamp. Handle it by the faces, never the edges.
Never tighten a bolt that passes through glass beyond finger-tight plus a small nudge.

steps.title: Top upside down on the cardboard
steps.say: Lay the top face-down on the flattened box. Sweep the floor first. One piece of grit under a table top leaves a scratch you will see forever.
do: Sweep, then lay the cardboard
Top face-down
Legs and hardware to hand

steps.title: Check whether the legs are angled
steps.say: Many tables have splayed legs. If the leg plate is angled, all four must lean outward in the same way. Hold each one up and look before you screw it.
do: Look at the leg plate: is it flat or angled?
Angled plates must all point outward
Hold two up and compare the lean
steps.watch: One leg mounted with its angle pointing inward makes the table rock and look wrong, and is very easy to do by accident.

steps.title: Screw the leg plates on, loose
steps.say: Position each plate on its holes, start every screw, and leave them all loose. Use only the short screws for anything going into the top.
do: Short screws into the top, longer bolts through the legs
Start all screws before tightening
Plates square to the table edges
steps.watch: Compare screw length to top thickness. This is the step where people put a screw through a brand new table top.

steps.title: Fit the lower shelf or stretcher
steps.say: If there is a lower shelf or a bar between the legs, fit it now while everything is loose. It is what stops the table racking.
do: Bolt both ends finger-tight
Check it is the right way up
Make sure it sits level
steps.tip: A lower shelf often doubles as the brace. Leaving it out because it looked decorative is why some tables wobble forever.

steps.title: Tighten diagonally, two laps
steps.say: Tighten opposite corners rather than going round in order. Then do a second lap, because the first one loosens its neighbors.
do: Opposite corners, in a cross
Shelf or stretcher last
Second full lap
steps.tip: Firm and stop. These tops are usually chipboard or MDF with a thin veneer and they strip very easily.

steps.title: Flip it and level it
steps.say: Lift it over rather than rolling it on a leg. Then press each corner and adjust the feet until it sits dead still.
do: Lift, do not lever
Press each corner to find the short leg
Screw that foot out, or add a felt pad
steps.tip: Felt pads on all four legs: protects the floor, stops the drag noise, and gives you a free way to shim the short leg.

steps.title: Fit the glass last, with two people
steps.say: Stick the rubber or suction pads on first, then lower the glass straight down onto them. Two people, handling it by the faces.
do: Clean pads stuck in position first
Two people, flat hands on the top and bottom faces
Lower straight down, do not slide it into place
steps.watch: Never slide glass across a frame or set its edge against anything hard. Tempered glass fails from edge damage, and when it fails it goes all at once.
steps.tip: Clean both the glass and the pads with glass cleaner first. Dust under a suction pad means the glass will shift.

steps.title: Load test and finish
steps.say: Press down firmly on each corner and the middle, then push sideways to check for rack. Any movement means one more tightening pass.
do: Press each corner and the center
Push sideways at the top
Retighten anything that moved
steps.tip: Re-tighten once more after a couple of weeks. New tables settle, and two minutes then saves a wobble later.

fixes.q: The table rocks on my floor
fixes.a: Find the leg that lifts, then either screw out its leveling foot or double up a felt pad underneath. Most floors are not flat, so this is normal and permanent.

fixes.q: The table racks sideways when I push it
fixes.a: The lower shelf or stretcher is loose or missing. That part is the brace. Tighten it, or check the parts list to see if you skipped it.

fixes.q: One leg sticks out at a different angle
fixes.a: An angled leg plate is mounted the wrong way round. Unscrew it, rotate it so the lean matches the other three, re-screw.
The rubber or suction pads are missing, dirty, or not stuck down. Clean the glass and the frame with glass cleaner, apply fresh pads, lower the glass straight down.

fixes.q: A screw went through the top
fixes.a: Wrong length screw. Back it out, fill with a colored wax repair stick, and use the short screws. Always compare screw length to top thickness first.
